subject: general
question: In how many languages was The Bal Sahitya Puraskar awarded in 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bal Sahitya Puraskar is awarded annually by the **Sahitya Akademi**, India's National Academy of Letters.
 
• In 2021, the Bal Sahitya Puraskar was conferred in **22 Indian languages**, covering a wide spectrum of regional and national linguistic diversity.
 
• The awards recognize and honor outstanding contributions in **children's literature**, including poetry, fiction, drama, and folk literature.
 
• The Sahitya Akademi promotes Indian literature across all languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Recipients are selected based on the literary merit and impact of their works on the cultural and intellectual growth of children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi**

 
 
• The Sahitya Akademi was established in 1954 and is dedicated to promoting Indian literature across diverse languages.
 
• It confers awards such as the Sahitya Akademi Award, Bal Sahitya Puraskar, and Yuva Puraskar annually.
 
• The Akademi also organizes literary events, seminars, and translations to foster cultural exchange among Indian languages.
 
 
 
• **Bal Sahitya Puraskar**
 
 
• Introduced by the Sahitya Akademi in 2010 to celebrate excellence in children's literature.
 
• Aimed at encouraging authors to create enriching literary works for young readers.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• It lists 22 officially recognized languages of India, including Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Kannada, and others.
 
• The Sahitya Akademi awards are conferred in all languages listed under the Eighth Schedule.
 
 
 
• **Children's Literature in India**
 
 
• Children's literature has a long tradition in India, with roots in folklore, epics, and moral tales.
 
• Modern writers have expanded this genre to include contemporary issues, adventure stories, and diverse themes.
